summary: Antoine Meillet worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Paris, Sorbonne, and EPHE under Darmesteter, Lévi, and Saussure. He held posts at EPHE, INALCO (1902–1906), and the Collège de France (1905–1936).

Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He held chairs in Arabic (1795) and Persian (1806) at INALCO, was professor at the Collège de France (1806–1838), and served as president of the Société Asiatique.
Antoine-Louis Henri de Polier was an Indologist who studied under the traditional teacher Ramchandra. He served as a colonel in the East India Company.

Antoine-Léonard Chézy worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Louis-Mathieu Langlès, worked at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, and held the chair of Sanskrit at the Collège de France from 1815 to 1832.

Anton Boller was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. From 1845, he served at the University of Vienna, becoming an extraordinary professor in 1850 and professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit in 1855.

Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca was an Indologist and linguist who completed his Dr. phil. at Humboldt University of Berlin around 1828–1831. He served as a Dozent there from 1849 to 1852 and held a post at the Royal Danish Library.

Anton Schiefner worked in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied law at Saint Petersburg State University and Oriental studies at Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding posts at Saint Petersburg First Gymnasium, Saint Petersburg Roman Catholic Theological Academy, and the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences.
Anton Westermann was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig between 1825 and 1830 and served there as co-director from 1830 to 1865.

Antonello Palumbo works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He held posts as a researcher at the Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2004) and at SOAS University of London (attested 2005–2010).

Antonino Forte worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Hōbōgirin (~1976–1986), the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1976–1984), the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~1982–1996), and as professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1989–2006).

Antonio T. de Nicolás worked in philosophy and Indology. He earned his PhD at Fordham University and served at Stony Brook University from around 1969 to 1996, where he became professor emeritus of philosophy.

Antonio Terrone works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter and Barend J. ter Haar, and also studied with traditional teachers. He has served as a scholar in residence at BDRC.
Anuj Misra is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Clemency Montelle and Kim Plofker, and held an external researcher post at the University of Copenhagen (attested 2026).

Anukul Chandra Banerjee worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned a PhD at the University of Calcutta, studying under Nalinaksha Dutt and Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya, later chairing Calcutta's Pali department and serving as Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.
Anuradha Seneviratna was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon from around 1965 to 1968 and later served there as a professor from around 1976 to 2003.
Anvita Abbi is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. She studied at Cornell University between roughly 1971 and 1975, and served on the editorial board at Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Archibald Edward Gough worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Monier Monier-Williams, was Anglo-Sanskrit Professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1868–1878), and served as Professor of Philosophy at Presidency University and Principal at Aliah University (~1881–1895).
Arghyadip Mondal is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and computational scholar who has been attested in 2026 as a PhD researcher and faculty member at Ghent University.
Ariane Macdonald is a Tibetologist who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. She held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 1972).

Arindam Chakrabarti works in philosophy and Indology. He earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford and held professorships at the University of Delhi, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Stony Brook University as an endowed chair.
